candidate_matches.title: Proxy trust through app.trustProxy applied by the core on every adapter
candidate_matches.diff_summary: C6b changes how req.remoteAddress()/req.isSecure() resolve when proxy trust is configured. FR-ENGINE-008 AC-2 says trusted mode = LEFT-most X-Forwarded-For entry (Express trust proxy=true) and rationale explicitly rejected trusted-address lists / hop counting ('reopen if a deployment needs hop counting'). C6b adds trustProxyHops/trustProxyCidrs that parse XFF from the RIGHT (by hops or first address outside trusted CIDRs). trustProxy(boolean) must stay unchanged (AC-1..AC-4 keep passing) with documented spoofing risk; AC-4 (decision made in DefaultRequest, no adapter reads X-Forwarded-*) must still hold. Needs a new 0.11.0 requirement that extends it, and the rationale 'rejected alternative' is now reopened.

candidate_matches.title: Server settings API: app.server(Configurer<ServerOptions>) and app.trustProxy
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Declares RestApp.trustProxy(boolean) under the NEW-state guard; AC-7 pins the RestApp method set in HttpApiSurfaceTest. C6b adds trustProxyHops(int), trustProxyCidrs(String...) and read accessors on RestApp (also NEW-guarded, Kotlin-callable): the RestApp surface test set changes and trustProxy(boolean) must remain source/binary compatible.

candidate_matches.title: Header, remote address, secure flag and Last-Event-ID accessors
candidate_matches.diff_summary: AC-2 pins that with the default configuration X-Forwarded-For/Proto/Forwarded are ignored and remoteAddress()/isSecure() equal the adapter values (stays true by default). C6a adds req.socketAddress() returning the real socket peer address regardless of proxy trust (so remoteAddress() may differ from socketAddress() once C6b trust is configured); this requirement is the natural anchor for the new accessor and its relation to remoteAddress().

candidate_matches.title: HttpAdapter SPI exchange data contract
candidate_matches.diff_summary: SPI gives the core 'the remote address and the secure flag' (remote address as a string-like value). C6a needs the real socket address from every adapter (TinyHttpd, in-memory, Servlet getRemoteAddr); verify whether the existing SPI value suffices or an add-only SPI member is required (mind CON-HTTP-004 engine-free SPI and IR-HTTP-007 add-only extension rule).

candidate_matches.title: Request and Response public surface of wave 3
candidate_matches.diff_summary: AC-1 lists the exact Request method set (incl. remoteAddress(), isSecure()); the set was re-pointed by later waves through HttpApiSurfaceTest (IR-APP-004 AC-3, FR-JSON, FR-COOKIE AC-8, FR-MULTIPART AC-6, FR-DX-*). C6a req.socketAddress() and C7 req.requestId() add two methods, so the exact-set surface test must be re-pointed to a 0.11.0 requirement with every earlier signature unchanged and @NonNull/@Nullable annotations (FR-KT-001, FR-KT-002, CON-HTTP-002 no Optional/java.util.function).

candidate_matches.title: HTTP request layer parameters and mount URL views
candidate_matches.diff_summary: AC-5 requires the request ID/start time to stay attached to the same request across nested layers; C7 req.requestId() must return that same stable id from any middleware/router layer.

candidate_matches.title: Standard error JSON body, status mapping and code values
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Defines the body {"error":{"code","message","requestId"}} (no whitespace, that field order), Content-Type application/json; charset=UTF-8, code values per status (400 BAD_REQUEST, 404, 405, 413, 415, 422, 426, 500, 501, 503, else HTTP_<status>) and AC-7 requestId == access-log rid. Auth failures (401/403/429 etc.) must reuse this shape; 401/403 are NOT in the listed code table (they fall to HTTP_401/HTTP_403) so the auth module either accepts HTTP_401/HTTP_403 or a new 0.11.0 requirement extends the code table (UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN) - a potential-update decision. C7 req.requestId() must equal this requestId.

candidate_matches.title: Only the core writes the standard error JSON, never through JsonCodec
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Auth error responses must go through HttpException/standard error writer (core) rather than the module hand-writing JSON through the codec; constrains how login/refresh/logout and middleware emit 401/403.

candidate_matches.title: Access log: one line per HTTP request, the WebSocket handshake and close lines, and the SSE stream-end line (wave 7)
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Request id (rid) of the access log line is the id C7 exposes via req.requestId(); AC-7 equality with the error body must hold. No change to the log format.

candidate_matches.title: Access log never records secrets and escapes control characters
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Keeps Authorization/Cookie header values, passwords, tokens and the query string out of the access log; the auth module (Bearer JWT, auth cookies, API keys, login body passwords) relies on it and its own logging must follow the same rule.

candidate_matches.title: Per-app state isolation and the NEW-state guard
candidate_matches.diff_summary: AC-3/AC-4 reject every RestApp/RouteBuilder registration and configuration method outside NEW with IllegalStateException through AppLifecycle.requireConfigurable. NOTE the premise 'registration after start rejected' is only partly true: FR-APP-021 AC-4 (0.10.0) permits ordinary HTTP route/middleware/RouteBuilder registration after listen, while config/ws/server-policy stay guarded. C4 (app.registrations(), app.onRegistration listener, validate -> listener -> apply -> record) and the auth 'install-before-routes' rule must be specified against this split: which registrations are allowed after start, whether onRegistration fires/records for post-start HTTP registrations, and that onRegistration/trustProxyHops/trustProxyCidrs themselves are NEW-state-guarded configuration methods.

candidate_matches.title: Ordered HTTP registration layers and persistent Route identity
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Core anchor for C4: HTTP route/middleware/router/error/static layers run in shared registration order (so an auth middleware must be installed before the routes it protects = install-before-routes rule), one Route identity per route(path) builder, atomic failure before a layer is published (AC-3), post-listen registration with safe snapshots (AC-4). app.registrations() read-only list and onRegistration listener must observe exactly these layers and preserve the atomicity: validate -> listener -> apply -> record, with a listener veto leaving nothing published and an in-progress request never seeing a partial registration.

candidate_matches.title: Every new RestApp or RouteBuilder configuration method calls the NEW-state guard first
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Each new configuration method (onRegistration, trustProxyHops, trustProxyCidrs; plus any auth install method) must call the guard first; registrations() and the trust accessors are read-only and unguarded like logger()/state().

candidate_matches.title: Middleware and Next interfaces and the middleware registration methods
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Auth enforcement is built on use(mw)/use(prefix, mw) and Middleware; C4 registration records must cover these overloads.

candidate_matches.title: Middleware scope and pipeline order in the dispatcher
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Original wave-4 pipeline-order rules; superseded in practice by FR-APP-021/FR-DX-008 ordered layers. Listed for ordering context only.

candidate_matches.title: 미들웨어를 전체 등록 순서로 실행
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Whole-registration-order middleware execution (now overridden/extended by FR-APP-021) is the basis of the install-before-routes rule for the auth middleware.

candidate_matches.title: 라우트 그룹으로 중복 prefix 제거
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Groups with prefix middleware are a registration path that app.registrations() / onRegistration must report (group ownership contract kept by FR-APP-021 AC-3).

candidate_matches.title: CORS 허용 출처·preflight 편의 설정 제공
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Typed CORS config; AC-4 says preflight terminates before downstream authentication, AC-5 WebSocket Origin separate, AC-6 Vary: Origin always. With cookie transport + CSRF the auth module must be installed after cors() so credentialed preflights are not 401'd; CORS allowedOrigins/credentials interplay with the CSRF Origin check needs an explicit relation. No change to CORS itself.

candidate_matches.title: Versioned common HTTP contract and retained legacy routing profile
candidate_matches.diff_summary: AC-7 retains the typed CORS extension; the versioned contract that 0.11.0 additions must not break (existing extensions/WS preserved).

candidate_matches.title: Origin check in the core before the upgrade extension point, same-origin default and allowlist
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Rationale notes cross-site WebSocket hijacking with cookies; cookie-transport auth makes this Origin check the CSWSH defence for ws routes. Auth module must not weaken or duplicate it; same-origin comparison uses Host (consider C6b trust interplay only if Host/proto derivation uses proxy trust - verify).

candidate_matches.title: Upgrade dispatch: middleware chain to completion, then the upgrade extension point, handler once after 101
candidate_matches.diff_summary: WS upgrades run the middleware chain first, so auth middleware also gates WebSocket upgrades (the 'authentication' in FR-APP-021 AC-6); the auth module must be compatible with the 426/401 order.

candidate_matches.title: Cookie value class and SameSite enum
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Cookie (getX/setX/isX, Kotlin properties) and SameSite {STRICT, LAX, NONE} are the building blocks of the auth cookie transport. No requirement or class named CookieOptions exists in the SRS; if the research design uses a CookieOptions type it is NEW (fluent cookie options exist only as FR-DX-005 AC-1 'HttpOnly Secure SameSite Path Domain' without a stated type name).

candidate_matches.title: res.addCookie serialises one Set-Cookie header per call
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Serialisation of Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite/Max-Age used by access/refresh/CSRF cookies; a SameSite=None-without-Secure rule, if the auth module enforces it, must be checked against this serialiser's validation.

candidate_matches.title: Lenient request-cookie parsing behind req.cookie and req.getCookies
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Request cookies parse leniently with attributes null/unset (path/domain/sameSite null); auth cookie reading (and duplicate-cookie handling) must tolerate this and not depend on attributes of parsed cookies.

candidate_matches.title: 쿠키 설정·옵션·삭제 편의 함수 제공
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Fluent cookie options and clearCookie (Max-Age 0 with matching Path/Domain) used for logout cookie clearing.

candidate_matches.title: req.body media-type, syntax, size, depth, UTF-8 and polymorphism checks
candidate_matches.diff_summary: req.body(Class) accepts only application/json and application/*+json (else 415); login/refresh bodies parsed through it get 415/400/413 behaviour, and a CSRF rule requiring a JSON Content-Type for cookie-auth mutations relies on this media-type check. No change.

candidate_matches.title: res.json encodes through the app codec and round-trips JSON values
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Token/response DTOs from login/refresh go through res.json and the JsonCodec SPI; auth module must stay Gson-free (CON-BUILD-013).

candidate_matches.title: Java 8 bytecode target for Java and Kotlin compilation
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Auth code in NaruServe-api compiles with release=8; JWT HS256 must use only javax.crypto Mac (HmacSHA256) / java.security, java.util.Base64 (API 26 is NOT allowed; Android 5.0 = API 21 lacks java.util.Base64 and java.nio.file) - verify against the animal-sniffer signature.

candidate_matches.title: Main dependencies of every module declared in wave 1
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Pins each module's main dependencies; 0.11.0 states 'no new dependencies' so the auth module inside NaruServe-api must add none (no JWT library, no bcrypt/argon library). Any password hashing must use JDK primitives (PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 availability on API 21 must be checked).

candidate_matches.title: animal-sniffer API 21 check on Android-bound modules
candidate_matches.diff_summary: NaruServe-api is checked against android-api-level-21; every JDK class used by utils.auth (Base64, MessageDigest.isEqual, SecureRandom, Mac, SecretKeyFactory algorithms, java.time, Objects, StandardCharsets) must exist in API 21. java.time and java.util.Base64 are out; the new package must be covered by the existing check without exemptions.

candidate_matches.title: Core isolation, servlet-free Android modules and single Gson version build checks
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Core (NaruServe-api) must not expose Gson/android/servlet types: the new utils.auth package inside NaruServe-api must serialise tokens without Gson types (own minimal JSON or the JsonCodec SPI), otherwise the build check fails.

candidate_matches.title: NaruServe-api main classes stay free of platform and adapter types
candidate_matches.diff_summary: utils.auth classes in NaruServe-api must not reference java.nio.file, CompletableFuture, java.net.http, android.*, servlet or TinyHttpd types (file-backed user/group/role stores must use java.io.File/streams).

candidate_matches.title: Maven group and Java package root
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Package root com.snoworca.naruserve; the new com.snoworca.naruserve.utils.auth package sits under it.

candidate_matches.title: Public API types avoid Optional, java.util.function, streams and java.nio.file
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Applies to every new public signature (registrations() list type, onRegistration listener functional interface, trustProxy* accessors, auth API): no Optional/java.util.function/streams/nio.file.

candidate_matches.title: Nullability check over the public API packages of NaruServe-api
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Reflection/annotation check covers public API packages of NaruServe-api; the new utils.auth package (and the new Request/RestApp methods) must be NullMarked and pass this check; package-info for utils.auth may need adding.

candidate_matches.title: Public method names of NaruServe-api avoid the Kotlin hard keywords
candidate_matches.diff_summary: All new public method names (auth API, registrations, onRegistration, trustProxy*) must avoid in/is/object/fun/when/val/var.

candidate_matches.title: Kotlin lambdas are accepted by every callback parameter without a DSL
candidate_matches.diff_summary: app.onRegistration listener and any auth callbacks/configurers must be @FunctionalInterface with Kotlin lambda tests (T11).

candidate_matches.title: Value objects follow getX, setX and isX naming so Kotlin property syntax compiles
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Auth value objects (User, Group, Role, ApiKey, options) must follow getX/setX/isX; req.socketAddress()/requestId() stay Express-style short names per CLAUDE.md.

candidate_matches.title: Loopback default bind, explicit LAN binding with warning, Host allowlist and bind outcomes
candidate_matches.diff_summary: AC-3 warning text tells the app to add its own authentication when binding non-loopback; the auth module is the framework's answer to this. The secure-transport rule (auth over plain HTTP) interacts with it: with no TLS listener (OPS-REL-006) secure-transport detection depends on isSecure()/trustProxy (C6b).

candidate_matches.title: TLS and WSS on the TinyHttpd adapter recorded as a post-v1 item with two reasons
candidate_matches.diff_summary: TLS listener is recorded as post-v1, so the auth 'secure-transport rule' (refuse/flag Secure cookies and credentials over non-TLS) can only be satisfied through req.isSecure() behind a trusted proxy (C6b) or an explicit dev override; the TLS statement in docs/api/defaults.md must not be contradicted.

candidate_matches.title: Servlet request mapping: raw path minus context path and servlet mapping, raw query, headers, and the same application types as on the embedded engine
candidate_matches.diff_summary: AC-3 asserts trustProxy takes effect in the core under the Servlet adapter (ServletRequestTest). C6a/C6b must also be exercised on the Servlet adapter (socketAddress from getRemoteAddr, hops/CIDR in core), keeping 'no adapter reads X-Forwarded-*'.

candidate_matches.title: Versioned bilingual common HTTP documentation
candidate_matches.diff_summary: 0.10.0 docs are bilingual (ko + en) with compile-checked Java 8/Kotlin examples; docs for registrations()/onRegistration, socketAddress, requestId, trustProxyHops/Cidrs and the auth module must follow the same bilingual rule and update docs/api/app.md, request.md, defaults.md and express-migration.md (app.set('trust proxy', n/CIDR) mapping) without invalidating old verified evidence.

candidate_matches.title: Wave 5 engine and server-setting decisions recorded in docs/api with defaults checked against the code
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Discarded (restated as OPS-ENGINE-002); historical docs requirement whose AC-4 maps app.set('trust proxy', ...) to app.trustProxy(...). Do not edit; 0.11.0 docs requirement should extend the current docs requirement instead.

candidate_matches.title: docs/api records the wave 5 engine decisions, with the WebSocket idle, ping and handshake rows settled by wave 7
candidate_matches.diff_summary: AC-4 pins the request.md proxy paragraph and the express-migration trust-proxy mapping with a docs test (WaveFiveDocsTest.appAndRequestNameServerTrustProxyAndKeeper); documenting trustProxyHops/Cidrs and the 'trustProxy(true) risk' must keep those verified assertions green (docs tests pin exact text).

candidate_matches.title: Every docs/api Java block compiles or sits on the named skip list
candidate_matches.diff_summary: New docs/api auth pages and the updated request/app pages must have compiling Java blocks (and Kotlin per FR-KT-004).

candidate_matches.title: A docs/api decision removes its marker in the same change and states its reason
candidate_matches.diff_summary: Governs (미확정) markers: any not-yet-decided auth API name in docs/api carries the marker and is removed when decided, per CLAUDE.md.

candidate_matches.title: TinyHttpd adapter implements HttpAdapter with confined engine types and per-feature classes, event-stream and upgrade paths filled (wave 7)
candidate_matches.diff_summary: AC-7 asserts the adapter remote address reaches the core unchanged (RawTargetSocketTest); C6a socketAddress builds on this value. Supersedes discarded FR-ENGINE-010 (same AC-5).

no_match_reason: No existing scope fits the auth/RBAC module itself. Grep for authentication/authorization/RBAC/JWT/password/CSRF/API key across all 16 scope SRS files finds only incidental mentions (access-log secret masking SEC-APP-001, loopback-bind warning telling the app to add its own authentication in FR-ENGINE-002, CORS preflight-before-auth in FR-DX-010 AC-4, Kotlin early-exit examples), and no requirement carries Target 0.11.0 yet. 01.product-architecture.srs.md (ARCH) is an empty template. Verdict: create a NEW scope for Auth (next free number is 17, e.g. docs/spec/17.auth.srs.md with a new prefix such as AUTH, via scaffold_scope; prefix not yet taken by any existing scope), and place the four Core changes as NEW 0.11.0 requirements in the existing scopes they extend: C4 in APP (05), C6a and C7 in HTTP (04), C6b in ENGINE (06), each extending (not editing) the verified blocks listed above. Docs requirements go to REL (15) or the new scope.
